title: Surjective pointed map from the neighbourhood colimit to the relative separable closure
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $y$ its image. Give $\Omega$ its $\kappa(y)$-algebra structure [def-weil-residue-field] via the residue embedding of $\bar y$. Write $K=\kappa(y)^{\mathrm{sep}}\subset\Omega$ for the relative separable closure [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure] and $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ for the chosen coordinate-ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. For any local-ring structure on $C$, there exists a surjective ring map $\psi:C\to K$ with kernel the maximal ideal, such that for every chosen representative affine pointed neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$, the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow\Omega)\circ\operatorname{Spec}\psi}\operatorname{Spec}C\xrightarrow{c_V}V$ equals $\bar v$. No residue-field equivalence, uniqueness, structural-map equation, or strict henselianity is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 04HX, with algebra.tex Tags 04GW and 04GP; online text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX and /tag/04GW and /tag/04GP

proof.text: Choose an affine chart through y. The equivalence of neighbourhoods over that chart with etale residue triples sends their residue embeddings into K, compatibly with pointed transitions. Identify the chart residue field with kappa(y); the assumed equation for the Omega algebra structure ensures this identification respects the embeddings.

source.place: Tag 04HX, with algebra.tex Tags 04GW and 04GP; online text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX and /tag/04GW and /tag/04GP

proof.text: The compatible triple maps give the surjective map psi with maximal-ideal kernel supplied by strictHenselization_triples. Transfer it along the colimit comparison, the affine-neighbourhood equivalence, and the small representative equivalence to the specified C. The maximal ideal is unique, so the kernel assertion holds for its given local-ring structure.

source.place: Tag 04HX, with algebra.tex Tags 04GW and 04GP; online text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX and /tag/04GW and /tag/04GP

proof.text: The specified effect of the triple equivalence on points and on coordinate-ring coprojections gives the factorization for neighbourhoods over the chart. Every affine neighbourhood receives a pointed map from one over that chart. Naturality of the canonical cone and the equation for a pointed morphism propagate the factorization to that neighbourhood and then to every chosen representative.
